proof_audit.judgment: Pass. Finite best/worst prize bounds follow by repeated independence. Strict calibration order, closed-cut existence (including zero endpoint), uniqueness and substitution establish an affine lottery index. The all-indifferent case is separated. Positive affine uniqueness concerns expected indices, not arbitrary ordinal transformations. The interval-wealth EU assumption is explicitly additional.

Pass. Finite CE existence uses continuity and strict increase on a common interval; binary Jensen gives the concavity converse. The C2 positive-derivative inverse formula has the correct Arrow–Pratt sign and both CE comparison directions. The local C3 proof first obtains CE-w=O(epsilon²) using a derivative bounded away from zero; fixed bounded shocks justify the uniform cubic remainder. The explicit log example has a stronger fourth-order error for separate algebraic reasons.

Pass. Summation by utility increments gives the correct FSD CDF direction and indicator converse. Negative lower-put utilities give SSD necessity; decreasing nonnegative secants give its affine-plus-negative-hinge sufficiency, including one/two atoms and the mean term. All real thresholds reduce to union knots plus constant outer differences. Increasing-concave order is not incorrectly restricted to equal means.

Pass. Endpoint truncation utilities bound X inside the Y support interval when means agree; constant Y is handled. Conditional-row constraints generate a compact convex marginal set. Nearest-point separation is proved by the right derivative on segments. Pair-support reduction gives a finite concave upper envelope with bounded slopes; adding Mx makes it increasing and equal means cancel M. Independent row maximization then contradicts separation. Numerical coupling and upper-hull witnesses support, but do not prove, this argument.

Pass. Zero-probability signals receive no posterior and contribute zero. Independent action rights and linear utility payoffs permit columnwise deterministic maxima. Ignore-information and statewise maxima bound value. The nonnegative loss decomposition proves zero gain iff one action is optimal at every positive posterior. Monetary fees can be directly subtracted only in the stated risk-neutral/additive-utility contract.

Pass. State-independent randomized garbling preserves every statewise action law. For the converse, the compact convex garbling image admits the proved nearest-point separator; uniform-prior payoffs nH, or H/pi for fixed full-support pi, supply a strict decision witness. A zero-prior state prevents that construction and the constant/perfect experiment counterexample is valid. Neither task accuracy nor posterior energy replaces all-payoff quantification.

Uniform Taylor and inverse mean-value steps justify the local order. Explicit symmetric-log rationalization proves the positive half-risk error below 1/1000 without extending the generic remainder.
Finite summation and indicator converse include zero masses at union support points. Strictly increasing utilities give strict shift preference; unequal means preclude a mean-preserving coupling.

Both lower-moment directions, conditional Jensen and the full finite equal-mean coupling converse are supplied, including support bounds, constant case and bounded envelope slopes. The sure-3 spread and crossing CDFs agree.
Every printed CDF/lower-moment knot and both variances agree. Opposite capped-utility rankings refute the assertion; adding any positive linear term preserves the differences because means coincide.
